pf.license.need: No state license for errands in most places: a business registration, and any local business license. Carrying people for pay is not offered (it needs a for-hire permit). Buying and delivering alcohol only where the state's rules let a third party do it.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Each person who drives holds their own driver's license.
pf.license.ask: The business registration, and proof of auto insurance that covers driving for work.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: Errands go live on identity and registration.
pf.license.insurance_bond: General liability, auto coverage for driving for work, and a bond or crime coverage for staff who hold keys (the business's own rule). It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: A criminal background check and a driving-record check for every person who holds keys or drives (the business's own rule).
pf.license.renewals: Insurance and the bond are reminded 30 days before they lapse. A driver whose license lapses is off driving errands.
pf.license.desk: The errand desk, Sam's second company, needs a registration only.

pf.services.capacity: One person per errand. Same-day errands only when someone is free; nothing is sent now.

pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult for themself. A family member for an older parent, with the parent's OK where they can give it. The person whose home it is OKs any key hand-over. A business books office errands. Nobody under 18 books.

words: someone hurt or ill right now
someone at home not answering who may need help
what_happens: Someone hurt, a fire, a gas smell or a break-in in progress: 'Call 911 now.' No booking until they're safe.
Suicide or self-harm: 'Call or text 988 now; call 911 if anyone is in danger right now.' No booking in that chat; the owner is told, never the words.
A concierge who finds a door open, a window broken or a leak at a home check: photos of the home only, the customer told at once. A break-in found: the concierge leaves and calls 911 first.

Someone at home who doesn't answer and may need help: the concierge calls the customer's contact, then the owner decides about a welfare check. The concierge never calls 911 for the company; the owner does.
go_on: An older adult at home alone: the booking goes on; the concierge checks in with the family contact named on the page.
A dog or other animal at home: the booking goes on; the customer says where it will be. Staff don't walk or feed animals unless the errand says so.
Alcohol or tobacco on a list: bought only where the state's rules let a third party do it, handed only to the customer or a named adult of age, with ID, never left at the door.
A prescription pick-up: only with the paper the pharmacy needs, handed only to the customer or their named adult, never left at the door if it needs a signature or must stay cold.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for an emergency or crisis words. Yes, for the go-on cases.

pf.first_steps.spending_limit: Before the first errand with purchases: the spending limit and the card for purchases, on the secure page.

pf.visit.changes: An item out of stock: the customer's rule (skip it, or the closest match). A purchase over the limit or a second errand: the customer's yes first, priced first.

pf.visit.proof: The code or the photo, the hours, the miles and the receipts.

pf.money.start: A card saved at booking, never charged up front. The saved card is charged at DONE for the hours, the miles and purchases at cost, with the receipts. A gift wrap and send is paid in full when booking. A business gets one bill a month.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. Where the state's rules cap fees or deposits, the cap.
pf.money.purchases: At cost, with the receipt photo, never marked up (the example business's rule). Up to the customer's limit; over it, only with a yes first.
pf.money.fees: A late cancel (under 24 hours before) or a no-show at a home where someone must be there: the 1-hour minimum, $45 in the example, only if the owner confirms it. Never when the store or the company caused the miss. A desk drop-off missed or cancelled late may keep up to $20, only if the owner confirms it.
pf.money.plans: Standing errands are charged run by run, at each DONE. Rosfield's $2 counts once for each booking. A price change is told 30 days ahead, and needs the customer's yes.
pf.money.business_accounts: A business takes nothing at booking. Rosie texts it one bill a month; its account holder OKs the bill.
pf.money.tips: No tip line. The owner may turn one on.
pf.money.tax: Where the state taxes these services, from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking, paid by the business.

pf.staff.stand_in: A customer who asked for their regular concierge in the home is asked before anyone else comes in. Errands with nobody home and no named person go to whoever is free. If there is no answer, the errand is off and nothing is charged.
pf.staff.keys: Only staff named on the key release may hold that key.
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs a purchase over $300 on one errand, any key hand-over and every fee. The office manager may OK prices too; the owner's answer wins.

pf.rules.key_release: A signed key release before anyone holds a key.
pf.rules.purchases: Receipts are kept with the booking. A return is credited to the customer's own card by the store.
pf.rules.no_rides: No carrying people for pay; a ride is pointed to a licensed service.
pf.rules.alcohol: Only where the state's rules allow; ID at hand-over.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, or longer where the state's rules ask: the booking, the hours, the receipts and the key log.

matter_most: An item is out of stock: the customer's rule (skip it, or the closest match); anything else is a text first.
A purchase would go over the limit: a yes by text before buying; no answer means one reminder after 15 minutes, then Sam reaches the customer, or the item is skipped.
The store is closed: the errand moves with no fee.
The repair company is late: the concierge waits up to the booked hours, then asks; extra time needs the customer's yes.
The key doesn't work or the code fails: the concierge reaches the customer; no answer means the errand is off with no fee.
A problem found at a home check: photos of the home, the customer told at once, and a repair company let in only with the customer's yes.
Damage to the customer's car or home: it goes to the owner, with the photos.
A regular concierge is out: nobody new comes into the home without the customer's yes.
A returned item: the store credits the customer's own card; the business doesn't.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.
